item.title: Google DeepMind, Meta, and Isomorphic Labs invest $300M in Biohub AI Initiative
item.description:
Google DeepMind, Meta, and Isomorphic Labs invest $300M in Biohub AI Initiative

Google DeepMind, Meta, and AI drug‑discovery startup Isomorphic Labs are jointly putting $300 million into Biohub, the nonprofit biomedical research organization founded by Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan. The money is part of a larger $1.8 billion effort to build AI datasets that let researchers ask, predict, and answer biological questions digitally, advancing a long‑term goal of a “virtual cell.”

🔍 Overview

  • Biohub was founded in 2016 to combat disease through large‑scale data‑driven biology.
  • The new investment will expand Biohub’s AI dataset creation to support a digital “virtual cell” that can be used for simulations.

💰 Funding & Partners

  • $300 million joint investment from Google DeepMind, Meta, and Isomorphic Labs.
  • $1.8 billion overall initiative to build AI datasets for biological research.
  • > $500 million from the U.S. Department of Energy over the next five years.
  • > $500 million in NIH‑contributed datasets, repositories, and knowledge bases from prior federal investment.
  • Additional “millions” from Google toward the virtual‑cell effort.

🧬 Goal: Virtual Cell & AI Datasets

  • Create AI‑driven datasets that enable scientists to ask, predict, and answer biological questions digitally.
  • Build a predictive model of biology that lets researchers perform experiments in silico.
  • Support disease prevention and management by allowing large‑scale computational simulations.

🗣️ Voices

“An accurate predictive model of biology could dramatically accelerate scientific discovery by enabling scientists to perform experiments digitally.” – Alex Rives, Biohub head of science

“The creation of a virtual cell is one of the most important challenges for the next era of science. It will require coordinated data generation efforts at a national and international scale, which is why these partners are coming together.”

#AI #Biotech #Funding #VirtualCell

Source: Google invests millions in Mark Zuckerberg’s efforts to create a ‘virtual cell’

item.title: BioDuro appoints Greg Makara to lead AI‑enabled discovery chemistry
item.description:
BioDuro appoints Greg Makara to lead AI‑enabled discovery chemistry

BioDuro, a global integrated contract research, development and manufacturing organization (CRDMO), announced on October 1 2026 that it has appointed Greg Makara, Ph.D., as Senior Vice President Lead Discovery Chemistry to strengthen early drug discovery capabilities.

🔎 Overview

  • The appointment supports BioDuro’s continued efforts to build a more integrated, data‑driven drug discovery platform.
  • It is part of BioDuro’s continued efforts to strengthen its early‑phase drug discovery and medicinal chemistry capabilities and integrate modern computational approaches more deeply across its discovery platform.

📅 Announcement Details

  • Location: Irvine, Calif.
  • Date: October 1 2026
  • Quote from BioDuro CEO Dr. Armin Spura: “This appointment builds on BioDuro’s broader efforts to incorporate AI and advanced computational tools into our drug discovery services.”

👨‍🔬 Leadership Background

Dr. Makara brings more than two decades of experience in drug discovery and chemistry leadership across pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and technology companies. His career highlights include:

Position Organization
Founder & CEO ChemPass
CEO & CTO (co‑founded chemistry service business) ComInnex, Inc.
Site Head AMRI Hungary
Leader, Target Validation Chemistry group Merck & Co., Rahway
Director (participated in ASMS screening technology ALIS) Neogenesis Pharmaceuticals

He has experience spanning library development, hit‑to‑lead and lead optimization, computer‑aided drug discovery and AI‑assisted drug discovery.

🤖 AI & Computational Chemistry Focus

In his new role, Dr. Makara will:

  • Lead the expansion of BioDuro’s computational chemistry, AI, and lead discovery capabilities.
  • Work across the discovery organization to support lead discovery projects and expand computational approaches, including:
    • Molecular modeling
    • Structure‑based drug design
    • Fragment‑based discovery
    • Virtual screening
    • Molecular design
    • Compound prioritization
  • Complement BioDuro’s experimental chemistry, biology, and DMPK expertise to help clients accelerate hit identification, lead generation, and optimization while making more informed decisions throughout early drug discovery.

Quote from Dr. Greg Makara: “BioDuro has built a strong foundation in chemistry, biology, DMPK, and integrated drug discovery, and I am excited to help further connect these capabilities with computational and medicinal chemistry. The combination of computational and experimental approaches can create a more efficient and informed discovery process. I look forward to working with BioDuro’s scientists and clients to apply these approaches to challenging drug discovery programs and accelerate the path from hits to optimized leads.”

🌐 Strategic Impact

  • The hire strengthens BioDuro’s integrated discovery platform with more powerful, data‑driven approaches.
  • Clients gain access to combined computational and experimental methods designed to speed early‑stage drug discovery.

#AI #DrugDiscovery #ComputationalChemistry #Biotech

Source: BioDuro Appoints Greg Makara as Senior Vice President | BioDuro

item.title: Microsoft Research Introduces Quine Multimodal World Model for Biology
item.description:
Microsoft Research Introduces Quine Multimodal World Model for Biology

Microsoft Research has introduced Quine, a research effort to create a multimodal world model of biology and an interactive harness that connects models, scientific tools, literature, and researchers.

🔍 Overview

Quine is designed to work across various biological boundaries, reflecting a vision for a discovery system that evolves through scientific use. It consists of two primary components:

  • A world model of biology: A system capable of representing the state of a biological system, predicting how that state evolves in response to interventions, and reasoning over the consequences of those interventions multiple steps into the future.
  • An interactive harness: A system that connects the world model to orchestration and reasoning models, scientific tools, literature, and research teams.

🧩 How it works

The core world model learns shared representations across biological modalities and scales, including:

  • Sequence
  • Structure
  • Function
  • Cellular state
  • Imaging data

By training across these modalities jointly, Quine can use evidence from one modality to inform predictions in another, capturing relationships that might be lost when separate single-domain specialist models are used. This integration allows researchers to generate predictions across modalities and reason about the consequences of biological interventions before wet-lab testing.

⚙️ Key details

Microsoft Research has applied Quine in collaboration with researchers at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard to study pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Through this work, they have used the system to prioritize compounds predicted to drive therapeutic tumor-state shifts and validated several top-ranked candidates across multiple wet-lab assays.

Quine is experimental research technology intended only for research, not for clinical or medical use. Its outputs may be incomplete or inaccurate and require review by qualified researchers and appropriate scientific and experimental validation.

🚀 Availability

  • Quine Fellows program: A cohort of scientists will be given access to the system to accelerate their research and provide scientific feedback.
  • Future Access: As the technology matures, Microsoft expects to expand access through products such as Microsoft Discovery.

#MicrosoftResearch #Biology #WorldModels #Biotech #AI

Source: Introducing Quine: An AI research system designed for the complexity of biology

item.title: FDA Approves Reduced Monitoring Time for Amgen IMDELLTRA Lung Cancer Treatment
item.description:
FDA Approves Reduced Monitoring Time for Amgen IMDELLTRA Lung Cancer Treatment

Amgen has announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved an update to the prescribing information for IMDELLTRA (tarlatamab-dlle). The update significantly reduces the recommended monitoring period for the first two doses of treatment for patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC).

⚙️ Key details

The new approval shortens the required monitoring time for patients receiving their initial infusions of IMDELLTRA in an appropriate healthcare setting. This change is based on an evolution in the administration of the therapy and reinforced by Amgen’s commitment to addressing real-world patient needs.

  • Monitoring Period Update: Patients are now monitored for 6 to 8 hours from the start of the first two infusions, a reduction from the previously recommended 22 to 24 hours.
  • Follow-up Assessment: Patients must receive an assessment, including vital signs, the day after each of the first two doses (Cycle 1, Days 2 and 9).
  • Proximity Requirements: For the first two doses, it is recommended that patients remain within one hour of an appropriate healthcare setting for a total of 48 hours from the start of infusion, accompanied by a caregiver.
Treatment Phase Monitoring Duration Requirement
First Two Doses (Cycle 1, Days 1 & 8) 6-8 hours
Third Dose (Cycle 1, Day 15) and Cycle 2 6-8 hours
Cycles 3-4 3-4 hours
Cycle 5 and Subsequent Doses 2 hours

🧩 How it works

IMDELLTRA is a first-in-class targeted immunotherapy indicated for adult patients with ES-SCLC whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy.

  • Molecular Binding: The therapy is engineered to bind to both DLL3 on tumor cells and CD3 on T cells.
  • Immune Activation: This dual-binding activates T cells to kill DLL3-expressing SCLC cells by forming a cytolytic synapse, resulting in the lysis of the cancer cell.
  • Target Specificity: DLL3 is a protein expressed on the surface of SCLC cells in approximately 85-96% of patients, but it is minimally expressed on healthy cells.

💡 Why it matters

Small cell lung cancer is an aggressive form of cancer where most patients experience disease progression after first-line treatment. Jay Bradner, M.D., executive vice president, Research and Development, Artificial Intelligence and Data at Amgen, noted that the time required for treatment and monitoring can add to the burden for both patients and care centers.

Reducing monitoring to 6-8 hours for initial doses addresses practical barriers, particularly for the 80% to 85% of U.S. cancer patients who receive care at community oncology practices. David M. Waterhouse, MD, MPH, FASCO, a medical oncologist at Oncology Hematology Care, stated that reducing the monitoring period makes the treatment more feasible for community practices, allowing patients to receive care closer to home and their support systems.

To manage risks such as cytokine release syndrome (CRS), IMDELLTRA is initiated using a step-up dosing schedule. Ongoing studies continue to evaluate reduced post-infusion monitoring across different indications and lines of therapy to inform future approaches.

#Oncology #Biotech #FDA #Immunotherapy #LungCancer

Source: FDA APPROVES REDUCED MONITORING TIME FOR FIRST TWO DOSES OF IMDELLTRA®

item.title: Compass Pathways Issues New Employee Inducement Grants Under Nasdaq Rule 5635(c)(4)
item.description:
Compass Pathways Issues New Employee Inducement Grants Under Nasdaq Rule 5635(c)(4)

Compass Pathways plc announced that it granted equity awards to thirty‑one newly hired non‑executive employees as a material inducement under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). The awards were granted on September 1, 2026.

🔍 Overview

  • Company: Compass Pathways plc (Nasdaq: CMPS), a biotechnology company focused on mental‑health treatments.
  • Grant date: September 1, 2026.
  • Purpose: Material inducement to employment, approved under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4).

📄 Grant Details

  • Recipients: 31 newly hired non‑executive employees.
  • Award types:
    • Options to purchase an aggregate of 280,600 shares.
    • Restricted share units or nominal‑cost options covering an aggregate of 133,500 shares for employees in the United Kingdom.
  • Exercise price: $13.24 per share, equal to the closing price of the Company’s American Depositary Shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on the grant date.
Award Type Shares Covered
Options 280,600
Restricted Share Units / Nominal‑cost options (UK) 133,500

⏳ Vesting Schedule

  • Options: 25 % vest on the first anniversary of the grant date; the remaining 75 % vest in equal monthly installments over the following three years, subject to continued employment.
  • Restricted Share Units / Nominal‑cost options: Vest in four equal annual installments, subject to continued employment.

✅ Nasdaq Compliance

  • The equity awards were approved by the Compensation and Leadership Development Committee of Compass’s Board of Directors.
  • The grants were made as a material inducement to each employee’s employment, satisfying Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4).

🧬 About Compass Pathways

  • Therapeutic focus: Development of COMP360, a proprietary synthetic psilocybin treatment under evaluation for treatment‑resistant depression (TRD) and post‑traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).
  • Regulatory designations:
    • Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for TRD.
    • Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway (ILAP) designation in the United Kingdom for TRD.
  • Clinical programs: Leading the world’s largest classic psychedelic clinical program in TRD and conducting a late‑stage trial for PTSD.

Forward‑looking statements – The press release contains forward‑looking statements regarding the company’s business strategy, clinical trials, regulatory approvals, and financial needs. These statements involve risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

#CompassPathways #Biotech #EmployeeGrants #Nasdaq

Source: Compass Pathways Announces New Employee Inducement Grants Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
